title: Florida House, District 119
what_it_does: Represents District 119 (Part of Miami-Dade) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Juan Porras
candidates.background: Juan Carlos Porras, a Miami native with a political-science degree from FIU, was elected in 2022 as one of the youngest legislators in Florida after working for Sen. Marco Rubio, Gov. Rick Scott and state lawmakers. He has focused on homeowners-association reform and sponsored a 2026 proposal to exempt seniors from non-school property taxes.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Porras voted for both 2026 property-tax measures and sponsored HJR 205 to exempt homeowners 65 and older from non-school property taxes.

candidates.name: Rey Sordo
candidates.occupation: Service worker, small-business owner and college student
candidates.background: Rey Sordo, 27, was born and raised in South Miami-Dade in a Cuban family. He works nights in the service industry, owns a small business and is a college student; his campaign theme is 'A Future We Can Afford.'

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

insurance.summary: Sordo calls for insurance reform that increases competition, holds insurers accountable and lowers costs while investing in resilience.
insurance.quote: We need real insurance reform that increases competition, holds insurers accountable, and lowers costs while investing in resilience to reduce future claims.

sources.title: Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Rey Sordo

housing.summary: He backs incentives for workforce housing near jobs and transit, renter protections against abusive fees, and rental-application transparency.
